newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania cenbank licences Greek private bank.
newsitem.headline: Albania cenbank licences Greek private bank.

text.p: Albania's central bank on Thursday issued a banking license to Greek-owned Tirana Bank, making it the first totally privately-owned bank to operate in Albania, state television reported.
Albania has so far issued licences to three foreign banks, two from Greece and one Malaysian-owned, in a bid to create a more effective banking system and draw in more foreign capital.
Tirana Bank is owned by a group of investors who also own Greece's Piraeus Bank. It has a founding capital of 200 million leks ($2 million).

The bank was allowed to take in deposits and make credits among other operations but was not authorised to deal in foreign exchange transaction until it doubled its capital, central bank officials said.
"But very soon they will increase their capital so that they can carry out all the activities the (Albanian) banking system law envisages," central bank governor Kristaq Luniku said.
